1 Introduction

This document describes the namespace for Intel® Innovation Platform Framework.

1.1 Terminology

TermDescription
APIApplication Programming Interface
IPFIntel® Innovation Platform Framework
JSONJavaScript Object Notification
OSOperating System
SDKSoftware Development Kit
Provider CollectionA repository selection of package representations for submission and publication; not a runtime provider object.
Collection versionThe version of a repository selection, independent of native provider versions and binary builds.
PackageA native implementation library, typically a DLL or .so, containing provider classes. Guide package names identify repository manifest stems, not verified library filenames.
Provider classA named native implementation with its own GUID, native provider version and schemas; not a runtime instance.
Native provider versionThe per-class version declared in the native manifest; not the collection version or minimum required IPF framework version.
Schema elementA property, command, event, parameter or nested field in a category schema.
Declared namespace placementThe documented location or location pattern of a provider class or schema element; not proof that an instance exists at runtime.
Provider instanceA runtime object created from a provider class with initialization configuration. A class can have multiple instances.

2 Overview

2.1 Scope

This document provides details of predefined namespace for the Intel® Innovation Platform Framework (Intel® IPF). This document pertains to only Intel® IPF Extensible Framework.

2.2 Audience

The audience for this document is Software Architects and Developers who intend to write applications for Intel platforms using Intel® IPF API.

2.3 Intel® IPF Client API

The following is the list of IPF Client APIs. The Client APIs are given here just for reference. Refer to the Client User's Guide for more details.

APIPurpose
QueryNode(path)Get the set of child nodes and properties for the node in the namespace. It also provides information on the type of properties.
GetNode(path)Returns a JSON result that contains the entire subtree which includes objects and properties for the specified Path. GetNode returns the entire tree under the path whereas QueryNode only gives immediate child nodes and properties of the Node.
GetValue(path)Returns the property for the specified path.
SetValue(path,value)Set the value of a property specified by "path", where path is the property to be set and the value. The value overload should be supplied to match the expected type of the property. The types supported are bool, int, double, string and char*. Properties can be read only, which will be specified in the JSON schema of the provider. The framework will reject SetValue calls on read only properties.
RegisterEvent(path, callback, context=nullptr)Applications use this method to register a callback for a given event. This api takes a path specifying the path of the event to register for, a callback function pointer, and an optional context pointer that will be returned when the event is raised. The callback is a language-specific function declaration. Callbacks take three parameters, the path and a JSON object describing the event and the context. Use GetSchema (path, SchemaType::EVENT) to query the events the path supports.
UnRegisterEvent(path, callback)Applications call this method to unregister from a given event. This api takes a path of the event that was registered for previously and the callback function pointer.
ExecuteCommand(path,command)Invoke a command on the specified path. The command parameter is a JSON string specifying the command name and any required parameters. Use getSchema(path, SchemaType::COMMAND) to query the commands the node supports.
GetSchema(path,schema_type)Get a schema describing the specified path. The schema_type specifies the type of schema that needs to be returned. The Schema types that will be supported by Namespace are Data, Event, Command and Result.
GetProperties()Returns the properties of the Client API.

3 Intel IPF Namespace

3.1 Predefined Namespace

The tables describe schema elements at declared namespace placements. The available, proposed and deprecated sections reflect PackageState projections, not verified runtime availability. Repository metadata and guide publication do not establish that a library was built or installed, or that a provider instance exists. Actual runtime presence and placement depend on the implementation, configuration and applicable conditions.

Array-valued declarations are marked with []. Explicit schema item paths retain {instance} as an element placeholder; placeholders already present in an accepted namespace placement are preserved. These are declared patterns, not concrete runtime instance names. Capability types are Get, Set, Get/Set, Command and Event. Capability descriptions come from the source. Consult the source schemas for additional details.

The minimum framework column is the selected collection requirement, not the introduction version of each capability or proof of runtime support.
